Subject: Unexpected charge line on Oct invoice — need usage lineage

Hi Mina,

Our finance team reviewed invoice INV-202610-AV and flagged an unexpected $9,200 line labeled "Overage - inference tokens". We expected October to be ~ $18k based on prior months; the overage jumped our bill to $27.2k. I've attached the invoice pdf and the usage export we pulled from your dashboard (avalabs_usage_oct2026.csv).

Two specific asks:
- Can you provide the provenance for the overage? We need to trace the tokens back to the originating request(s) or job(s) (session IDs, timestamps, and request paths).
- If this is due to a replay or test-run from our staging environment, we need that line item removed or credited.

Quick context: we run nightly backfill jobs from our analytics cluster (internal id: backfill-az1) but those were supposed to be on our sandbox account. We did not expect production metering to pick them up.

We appreciate a fast turn-around — month-end close is next Friday for Avalabs. If you need authorization to pull deeper traces, procurement@avalabs.ai is copied.

Thanks,
Ava

- Time window: 2026-10-14 01:10:00 -> 2026-10-14 03:05:00 UTC (spike window matches Avalabs' csv)
- Attribution: ~1.12M additional generation tokens attributed to customer_id: AV-9382 on pool prod-gpu-a.
- Root cause hypothesis: a scheduled backfill job (internal id backfill-az1) executed against your API key instead of the sandbox key. The job performed batched requests with long context (avg seq_len ~2,400), which explains the token count.
- Evidence: we have matching request_ids and ephemeral container ids in the session_traces_20261006.jsonl (attached to this thread).

Proposed next steps:
1) Provisional credit: compute token-to-dollar using the October rate card; preliminary math points to a credit of $8,950 (close to the $9.2k overage line — small rounding/tax difference remains).
2) Tax handling: Kimberly, this will be a retroactive adjustment to INV-202610. Avalabs may need a corrected invoice and credit memo; please advise on VAT/tax treatment for US vs EU entities.
3) Prevent recurrence: add a policy check to block prod API keys from being used by long-running batch jobs; Ops ticket created (OPS-2118).

Let me know if you want me to draft the credit memo and the corrected invoice.

Subject: Re: Unexpected charge line on Oct invoice — resolution and next steps

Hi Ava — quick update and resolution summary. Thanks for your patience while we investigated.

What we found:
- Root cause: an internal backfill job (backfill-az1) executed against an Avalabs production API key on 2026-10-14 UTC. The job issued ~1.12M extra generation tokens with long contexts (avg seq_len ~2400). We matched request_ids in your usage CSV with session traces in our logs.
- Attribution: the calls were billed to AV-9382 (production) rather than your sandbox.

What we’re doing:
- Credit: Redwood will issue a provisional credit of $8,950 against INV-202610. The credit will be posted as a "Billing Adjustment / Overcharge Correction" and you should see it reflected on your next statement. A corrected invoice and credit memo will be provided.
- Tax/VAT: Kimberly (cc) confirms that because the original invoice was issued to your US entity, the credit memo will be processed against that same entity. If Avalabs wants the activity to be reclassified to an EU entity for VAT reasons, procurement must provide the target billing entity and tax IDs so we can process a reissuance.
- Evidence: I’ve attached a redacted session excerpt (session_traces_20261006.jsonl) that shows the request_id mapping and timestamps. We can provide additional traces under NDA if you need more granularity.
- Prevention: Ops will update policy to prevent prod-key execution for long-running batch jobs (OPS-2118).

Next steps / asks for you:
1) Confirm acceptance of the $8,950 provisional credit.
2) If you require reissuance to an EU entity for VAT, reply with the entity name and tax ID.
3) Let us know if you want the raw traces shared over an encrypted transfer.

Again, apologies for the disruption; we’ll fast-track the credit and corrected paperwork.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Manager — Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
